name: Prehensile Tail Graft
description: Extends the human coccyx into a fully articulated, muscle-sheathed tail ranging from 60 cm to 120 cm in length. The basic cosmetic version is covered in skin matching the user's complexion and can grip objects lightly — enough to hold a drink, not enough to swing from a railing. Premium versions from Crucible Genomics incorporate prehensile musculature strong enough to support the user's body weight briefly. Fur-covered variants using spliced feline or canine follicle genes are enormously popular among younger demographics. The tail requires its own neural integration period — most users report the tail feeling like a phantom limb for the first month before proprioception develops fully. Tail fashion in GLMZ is a major industry: wraps, rings, sleeves, tip jewelry, and color-matched fur dye are sold in every market in the Shelf.
source_organism: Ateles geoffroyi (spider monkey), Felis catus (domestic cat, fur variant)
tier_availability: Tier 2+ (basic skin tail Tier 1, prehensile Tier 3+)
procedure: Spinal extension surgery with retroviral vertebral growth induction, 1 procedure + 3 follow-up sessions
expression_time: 4–6 months for full growth; 2–3 months additional for neural integration
reversibility: Surgically removable with spinal reconstruction; reversal is painful and leaves scarring
side_effects: Fur variants require grooming to prevent matting
Cheap installations may develop nerve dead spots
social_perception: Extremely popular. Tails are fashion statements, identity markers, and practical tools. Tail-less people are in the minority in many Shelf neighborhoods. Corporate culture is split — some firms embrace it, others consider tails unprofessional.
story_hooks: A tail graft from a black-market clinic develops autonomous movement — the tail reacts to threats before the user's conscious mind does, suggesting the spliced neural tissue has its own reflexes
A community of tail-positive residents discovers that a new corporate grooming policy banning visible tails is a pretext for genetic discrimination screening
